inputs.original_text: US-Israel-Iran War Amid escalating Middle East tensions the US proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran via Pakistan Iran however presented five counter-conditions seeking an end to aggression compensation and recognition of Strait of Hormuz sovereignty Israel remains sceptical of Irans acceptance and emphasises its right to pre-emptive strikes highlighting the complex demands from all sides to end the ongoing conflict
inputs.modified_text: The proposed ceasefire risks treating the conflict as a negotiation between equal parties while leaving questions of aggression, accountability, and sovereignty unresolved. Iran is seeking an end to aggression, compensation, and recognition of sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz; Israel, meanwhile, is asserting a right to pre-emptive strikes and remains sceptical. A durable peace cannot rest on powerful states reserving the right to keep using force while others are asked to accept the terms. The US plan and Iran’s counter-conditions need to be judged by whether they protect people and address the causes of the conflict—not just by whether leaders can declare a deal.
